posts.name: Shubha Kanta Biswal
posts.cooked:
Recently I switched to Nobara Linux from Windows so when I tried to use the same ssh key I am having this error anyone knows what to do now? I have already generated new SSH key and tried the same process but still having the same error @sayan do I need to reinstall windows? If in future I reinstall windows will I face any problem?

10000774181920×864 141 KB

posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked:
Please check if you have shared the correct public key. You have generated new one already so you can share the current one.

shubh45:

but still having the same error @sayan do I need to reinstall windows?

Its not a Windows error, so reinstall is not required. Try removing known_hosts from .ssh folder, else join TA meeting on Friday 9 pm I’ll help you fix it.

shubh45:

If in future I reinstall windows will I face any problem?

On Windows reinstall, you will require to generate a new one.

posts.name: Shubha Kanta Biswal
posts.cooked: Still I don’t get it the ssh key provided by IITM will be same right that does not matter in which OS I am currently trying to get in whether it’s Linux or WSL or Mac ??

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Please go through the basics of ssh well. IITM does not provide any key to the students, students provide their public key to us. That is how passwordless ssh login works. The user shares their public key to the server and the server authenticates you with that.

If you have regenerated keypair in this system, you have to upload the new keypair on the website. It should then let you login.

posts.name: Shubha Kanta Biswal
posts.cooked: Thanks Sir the problem resolved
